start.name: Meleiha concession production areas (Merged Meleiha license, Western Desert) — one of six production areas the pipeline gathers from; no single named area could be pinned
start.coord_source: OpenStreetMap Nominatim geocode of 'Meleiha, Egypt' (village/field label in Matrouh governorate), corroborated by an academic reservoir-study description of the Meleiha concession centered near 30°45'N, 27°03'-27°05'E — same location within ~5 km. This is the general Meleiha concession anchor, NOT a specific one of the six production areas.

end.name: Meleiha new gas processing plant / early production facility (Agiba Petroleum, within the Merged Meleiha concession)
end.coord_source: Same OSM Nominatim anchor as start — no separate coordinate exists for the plant itself; it sits within the same concession footprint (700 km2 block, per Wood Mackenzie/industry reporting).

corridor_note: This is NOT a point-to-point trunk line and a great-circle 'endpoints' model does not fit it. Independent reporting (egyptoil-gas.com, quoting the Petrojet/SLB contract scope; and Youm7/Attaqa on the same Phase II project) is explicit that the 20-inch, 130 km gas pipeline is a GATHERING network that 'connects six production areas to the new gas processing station' at Meleiha field, run in parallel with a separate 122 km / 19-well flowline network. All of this — the six production areas and the new processing plant — sits inside the single ~700 km2 Merged Meleiha concession (Agiba Petroleum, Eni/IEOC 76% + Lukoil 24%, EGPC carry), roughly 290 km SW of Alexandria and ~130 km north of Siwa Oasis. The cumulative 130 km therefore reflects branching gathering-line length across six wellhead clusters, not the separation between two termini. GEM's row already logs 'Western Desert' at both ends, which is consistent with this reading. We could not find a named location for any individual one of the six production areas, nor a distinct name/coordinate for the new gas plant beyond 'Meleiha field' itself.
length_check: Sheet length (130.0 km) matches the reported pipeline scope exactly (Petrojet/SLB contract: '20-inch, 130 km' gas pipeline) across three independent outlets (egyptoil-gas.com, Youm7, Attaqa). The 130 km is the network's own stated length, not a straight-line distance we independently verified against two coordinates — there are no two coordinates to check it against, per the corridor_note above.
notes: Do not draw this as a single great-circle segment. If §8 routing must produce something, the honest options are either (a) skip P8070 for the endpoints rung and flag it for a human with access to a Meleiha field development map showing the six production-area names, or (b) draw it as a single point/stub at the Meleiha concession anchor with RouteAccuracy no better than 'very low' and a note that it represents a gathering hub, not a trunk. National-grid connection via the 'Western Desert Gas Complex' near Alexandria (mentioned in Eni's 2021 Meleiha/Meleiha Deep merger release) is a SEPARATE, much longer piece of infrastructure downstream of this plant — do not conflate it with this 130 km pipeline; the 290 km Meleiha-to-Alexandria distance would be wildly inconsistent with a 130 km pipe.

start.name: NORPETCO fields, North Bahariya concession (Abrar / Abrar South / Ferdaus / Ganna / Rawda / Rayan — six producing fields on two development leases, North Bahariya Petroleum Company, a Sahara North Petroleum / IPR joint venture)
start.coord_source: NOT PINNED. Multiple sources place the concession qualitatively — 'eastern extension/eastern flank of the Abu Gharadig Basin,' 'close to Apache's East Bahariya block,' 'between El Fayoum and the Qattara Depression,' and '190 km SW of Cairo' (SPE-164693-MS abstract, paywalled/403 on this session so not cited as a ref) — but none of the six field names geocode in OpenStreetMap Nominatim (tried Abrar, Rayan; both returned unrelated street-name matches in Egyptian cities, not the oil field), and no source gives a numeric lat/lon. Per the hard rule against substituting a nearby town or inventing a coordinate, this is left null.

end.name: Abu Gharadig field / Khalda Petroleum Company operating area (the pipeline's 'Abu Gharadig' namesake)
end.coord_source: OpenStreetMap Nominatim geocode of 'Abu Gharadig, Egypt' (two independent hits within ~1 km of each other, Arabic and English labels both resolving to the same village/field point), which sits inside the academically reported Abu Gharadig field bounding box (29°35'-30°00'N, 28°20'-28°50'E) — two independent corroborating sources for the location.

corridor_note: Identity of the pipeline is well supported even though coordinates are not: egyptoil-gas.com (2026) reports NORPETCO 'extending a 27 km gas pipeline between NORPETCO's and Khalda Petroleum's fields' at a cost of $3.8 million, to displace diesel with gas and cut trucking risk — a length match to GEM's 27.0 km to the digit. 'Abu Gharadig' in the GEM pipeline name almost certainly refers to Khalda Petroleum's Abu Gharadig-area operations (Khalda operates across the Abu Gharadig Basin, and the North Bahariya concession sits on the basin's eastern flank immediately adjacent to it), not a separate 'Badr El Din/BAPETCO' entity — consistent with the batch's standing note that 'Badr El Din Company' = BAPETCO the operator, a different actor entirely.
length_check: 27 km sheet length matches the egyptoil-gas.com report of a 27 km NORPETCO-Khalda pipeline exactly. Since North Bahariya sits on the immediately adjacent eastern flank of the Abu Gharadig Basin (not a distant basin), a ~27 km separation between a North Bahariya field and the Abu Gharadig field/plant area is geologically plausible, though we could not verify it against a second coordinate.
notes: Only one endpoint (Abu Gharadig) is pinnable. The NORPETCO end needs a field-level map (e.g. an EGPC concession map or a Khalda/Apache field atlas) naming which of the six North Bahariya fields — Abrar, Abrar South, Ferdaus, Ganna, Rawda, or Rayan — the pipeline actually starts from; a reviewer with such a map could resolve this quickly. Do not default to the Abu Gharadig point for both ends.

start.name: Fayoum (city/governorate) — candidate anchor only; NOT confirmed as this pipeline's actual endpoint

end.name: Giza (city/governorate) — candidate anchor only; NOT confirmed as this pipeline's actual endpoint, and more likely a mis-parse of the 'Giza Canal' (ترعة الجيزة) that the nearest identified real project runs alongside within Fayoum governorate

corridor_note: We could not find a 27 km 'Fayoum-Giza' gas pipeline in any English or Arabic source, and the straight-line distance between Fayoum city and Giza city is roughly 60-70 km by road corridor, not 27 km — inconsistent with a literal city-to-city trunk at this length. The closest real, well-documented project is Egypt's Ministry of Petroleum Decision No. 1884/2025 (25 Dec 2025) approving THREE natural-gas distribution lines for Fayoum governorate at 70 bar, 24-inch/16-inch, totaling 40.5 km: (1) Beni Suef - New Fayoum City, 24-inch, ~19 km, whose route explicitly runs 'parallel to the Giza Canal (ترعة الجيزة) and the Giza Right Bank feeder canal' within Fayoum governorate before crossing into New Fayoum City; (2) a 16-inch Fayoum-expansion line, ~12 km; (3) a 16-inch Itsa-supply line, ~9.5 km. None of the three individually is 27 km, and the project is named for Beni Suef and Fayoum, never 'Giza' as an endpoint city — the 'Giza' reference in the sourced material is a CANAL name (an irrigation feature that runs through Fayoum governorate), not the city of Giza 60+ km away. It is plausible GEM's 'Fayoum-Giza' name is a corruption or shorthand of this canal-parallel corridor, or refers to a different, not-yet-found project entirely.
length_check: Sheet length (27.0 km) does not match any of the three segments in the one closely-related project found (19 km / 12 km / 9.5 km, totaling 40.5 km), and is far short of the true Fayoum city-to-Giza city road distance (~60-70 km). This inconsistency is itself evidence the pipeline is NOT a literal Fayoum-city-to-Giza-city trunk.
notes: Flagging for a reviewer rather than guessing: this needs either (a) the actual GASCO/EGAS project document behind GEM's 'Fayoum-Giza' name (possibly an older or different-numbered project than the Dec 2025 one found here), or (b) confirmation from Baird/a researcher with Arabic petroleum-ministry-decision archives on what 'Fayoum-Giza' specifically denotes in Egyptian gas-grid nomenclature. The coordinates given above are city-center anchors for orientation only and should NOT be used to draw a route without that confirmation.
